name: Consolidated Telcom
old_description: Consolidated is the premier provider of telecommunication services in Southwestern North Dakota since 1961. Customer service is our main priority, from customer service representatives, internet and service support, to our technicians in the field. You, our customer, are our number one priority, 24/7/365.
about:
Consolidated Telcom, headquartered in Dickinson, North Dakota, traces its roots to January 2, 1961, when the Bowman‑Slope Rural Telephone Mutual Aid Corporation and the Dunn Telephone Mutual Aid Corporation merged to form the Consolidated Telephone Cooperative. The cooperative is owned by its members—customers who use its services—and governed by an elected board of directors.

The company provides telecommunications services across southwestern North Dakota, including fiber‑to‑the‑home internet, cable television, voice, and business services such as cybersecurity and camera solutions. Since 2005 it has built a 100% fiber‑to‑the‑home network in its cooperative exchanges, serving 19 communities, and is extending fiber upgrades to its competitive local exchange carrier (CLEC) territory in Dickinson, Belfield, and Gladstone. Operations also include a CATV system acquired in 2000 that now covers the entire cooperative service area.

Consolidated serves residential and business customers in rural and small‑town markets across southwestern North Dakota. Its customer base includes households, farms, ranches, and enterprises such as Dickinson State University, which became its first CLEC client in 1998. The cooperative model aims to deliver urban‑level services at affordable rates to communities that larger carriers often overlook.

Founded to bring essential telephone service to areas where commercial providers found it unprofitable, the cooperative remains driven by its mission to “empower our communities by delivering advanced telecommunications products and services and building reliable, future‑ready infrastructure.” Its structure returns revenues above operating costs to members as capital credits, aligning incentives with customer needs rather than shareholder profit.
